author: agent
text:
WHY THIS IS THE READINESS ITEM AND NOT A MODELLING NICETY. Recorded 2026-09-16 from a scenario run: sudden large-scale adoption where presence is required rather than optional.

Today this bead reads as an accuracy problem. Under any deployment where a presence level is a REQUIREMENT someone must satisfy, it becomes a fraud-prevention problem, because it is the only thing standing between the vocabulary and a market for faking it.

The mechanism: presence becomes a number everyone wants to be as high as possible, and a consumer holding the credential has no way to check anyone's work -- it sees presence=hardware in a hint and takes the daemon's word. The first implementation that returns hardware off a software timer seeded at login passes, and passes permanently, because there is nothing in the credential a relying party could examine to catch it. persona-3tly.2 makes it worse: with user presence and user verification collapsed into one level, even an honest implementation cannot distinguish 'someone touched the key' from 'someone proved they are the enrolled human', so they get sold as the same number.

That is the difference between shipping a weak claim and shipping the vocabulary that a false claim is made in. If hire defines presence=hardware and provides no way to verify it, hire is the laundering mechanism.

CONSEQUENCE FOR SEQUENCING, and it is the one place the roadmap's 'presence last, deliberately' order has a real exception. Presence does not need to SHIP early. But either the assertion reaches the consumer, or the hint stops emitting a level above session. Refusing to say a thing is always available and costs nothing, and that is the cheap half of this bead which could land any time.

BLOCKS persona-2myu.2: the presence half of a conformance suite cannot be written until there is an assertion for the suite to check.
